The Fourth Adhyāya of the First Aṣṭaka

Sūkta 47 — "ayaṃ vāṃ madhumattamaḥ"

original p. 1

Fourth sūkta of the Ninth Anuvāka; first of the Fourth Adhyāya.

Forty-seventh Sūkta no separate title line is printed at the head of p. 1: the sūkta begins directly under the Adhyāya title; the heading block with "Sūkta — 47" is on p. 2

original p. 1

title of the Fourth Adhyāya, Sāyaṇa's introduction, and the beginning of the Kannada anuvāda

Printed on the page: the Om emblem; śrī mahāgaṇādhipataye namaḥ; the series title Sāyaṇabhāṣyasahitā Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, Bhāga 5 (the Kannada numeral reads "೫"); the heading prathamāṣṭake caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ with its Kannada rendering "modalaneya aṣṭakadalli nālkaneya adhyāyavu" ("the fourth adhyāya in the first aṣṭaka"); and the same six verses of homage as in the earlier volumes.

वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननम् ॥ यस्य निःश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वन्दे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरम् ॥ वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायी सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥

vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānām upakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syus taṃ namāmi gajānanam || yasya niḥśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tam ahaṃ vande vidyātīrthamaheśvaram || vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyī sadāśivaḥ | tasmāt sarvaprayatnena vedam eva sadā japet ||

Translation the same verses as in Volume 4, editorial and tentative: "May the gods headed by Vāgīśa (Brahmā), by bowing to whom, at the start of all undertakings, men have their aims accomplished — to that elephant-faced one I bow. I salute Vidyātīrtha-Maheśvara, whose breath is the Vedas and who created the whole world from the Vedas. The Veda is Śiva and Śiva is the Veda; the reciter of the Veda is Sadāśiva. Therefore with every effort one should always repeat the Veda alone."

Sāyaṇa's introduction printed in Kannada script; read from the 150-dpi image; the words marked [?] are crowded

अथ प्रथमाष्टके चतुर्थोऽध्याय आरभ्यते । अयं वामिति नवमानुवाकस्य चतुर्थं सूक्तं दशर्चम् । अत्रानुक्रान्तं । अयं दश प्रागाथं त्रिति [?] । ऋषिश्चान्यैरिति [?] परिभाषितत्वात्कण्वपुत्रः प्रस्कण्व ऋषिः । तथा पूर्वत्राश्विनं त्रित्यृक्तत्वात्तेह्यादिपरिभाषयेदमपि सूक्तमश्विदेवताकं [?] । अनयैव परिभाषयेदमुत्तरं च प्रागाथं । अतः प्रथमातृतीयाद्या आयुजो बृहत्यः । द्वितीयाचतुर्थाद्या युजः सतोबृहत्यः ॥ प्रातरनुवाक आश्विने क्रतौ बार्हते छन्दस्येतत्सूक्तं । अथाश्विन इति खण्डे सूत्रितं । इमा उ वामयं वां । आ. ४-१३ [?] । इति ॥ आश्विनशस्त्रेऽस्यैतत्सूक्तं प्रातरनुवाकन्यायेन । आ. ६-५ [?] । इत्यतिदिष्टत्वात् ॥

atha prathamāṣṭake caturtho 'dhyāya ārabhyate | ayaṃ vām iti navamānuvākasya caturthaṃ sūktaṃ daśarcam | atrānukrāntaṃ | ayaṃ daśa prāgāthaṃ triti [?] | ṛṣiś cānyair iti [?] paribhāṣitatvāt kaṇvaputraḥ praskaṇva ṛṣiḥ | tathā pūrvatrāśvinaṃ trityṛktatvāt tehyādiparibhāṣayedam api sūktam aśvidevatākaṃ [?] | anayaiva paribhāṣayedam uttaraṃ ca prāgāthaṃ | ataḥ prathamātṛtīyādyā āyujo bṛhatyaḥ | dvitīyācaturthādyā yujaḥ satobṛhatyaḥ || prātaranuvāka āśvine katau bārhate chandasy etat sūktaṃ | athāśvina iti khaṇḍe sūtritaṃ | imā u vām ayaṃ vām | ā. 4-13 [?] | iti || āśvinaśastre 'syaitat sūktaṃ prātaranuvākanyāyena | ā. 6-5 [?] | ity atidiṣṭatvāt || Crowded: the Anukramaṇikā clause "ayaṃ daśa prāgāthaṃ …", the parenthetical references to the "paribhāṣā", and the word "kratau" — printed so that it reads like "katau"; all [?].

Translation editorial and tentative: "Now the Fourth Adhyāya of the First Aṣṭaka begins. 'Ayaṃ vām' is the fourth sūkta of the ninth anuvāka, of ten ṛks. The Anukramaṇikā here: 'ayaṃ daśa prāgāthaṃ …' [?]. The ṛṣi is Praskaṇva, son of Kaṇva, as fixed by the convention [of the Anukramaṇikā] [?]. And since the preceding was said to be Āśvina, by the convention [?] this sūkta too has the Aśvins as deity. By the same convention this and the next are Prāgātha; hence the first, third, and following odd ṛks are Bṛhatī, the second, fourth and following even ṛks Satobṛhatī. In the Prātaranuvāka, at the Āśvina rite, this sūkta is used in the Bārhata metre; it is prescribed in the section 'athāśvina': 'imā u vām, ayaṃ vām' (Āśv. 4-13 [?]). In the Āśvina-śastra it is used by the rule of the Prātaranuvāka, since this is extended there (Āśv. 6-5 [?])."

Anuvāda (Kannada), pp. 1–2 — "Ayaṃ vām is the fourth sūkta in the ninth anuvāka. It has ten ṛks. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated that the ten ṛks of this sūkta are in the Prāgātha metre. The ṛṣi of this sūkta is Praskaṇva, the son of Kaṇva. The Aśvin gods are the deities of this sūkta. 'Prāgātham bārhatam' as a metre means, according to the paribhāṣā sūtra, [that] the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth ṛks are in the Bṛhatī metre; the third [sic: evidently the second], fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth ṛks are in the Satobṛhatī metre. When the mantras of the Bṛhatī-metre in the mantras that have the Aśvin gods as deity in the Āśvina-kratu are recited at the time of reciting the mantras of the Prātaranuvāka, this sūkta is recited. This matter is stated in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta-sūtra in the section 'athāśvina' by the sūtra 'imā u vām ayaṃ vām' (Ā. 4-13 [?]); and in the same Śrauta-sūtra it is said that at the time of reciting the Śastra mantras of the Aśvin gods this sūkta is to be used as Prātaranuvāka mantras (Ā. 6-5 [?])." The Kannada numeral for the second group of Satobṛhatī ṛks, "೩, ೪, ೬, ೮, ೧೦", reads like "3" where "2" is meant; kept as read.

॥ ॐ ॥

सूक्त — ४७ ॥ मण्डल — १ ॥ अनुवाक — ९ ॥ सूक्त — ४७ ॥ ॥ अष्टक — १ ॥ अध्याय — ४ ॥ वर्ग — १, २ [?] ॥ ॥ सूक्तदल्लिरुव ऋक्संख्यै — १० ॥ ॥ ऋषिः — प्रस्कण्वः काण्वः ॥ ॥ देवता — अश्विनौ ॥ ॥ छन्दः — प्राग्गाथं बार्हतं । १, ३, ५, ७, ९ बृहती । २, ४, ६, ८, १० सतोबृहती ॥

sūkta 47 | maṇḍala 1 | anuvāka 9 | aṣṭaka 1 | adhyāya 4 | varga 1, 2 [?] | ṛks 10 | ṛṣi: Praskaṇva Kāṇva | devatā: the Aśvins | chandas: Prāgātha–Bārhata — Riks 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 Bṛhatī; Riks 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 Satobṛhatī. The varga numerals are small and read with doubt.

original pp. 2–6

Rik 1

Saṃhitā-pāṭha accents not reproduced

अयं वां मधुमत्तमः सुतः सोम ऋतावृधा । तमश्विना पिबतं तिरोअह्न्यं धत्तं रत्नानि दाशुषे ॥ १ ॥

ayaṃ vāṃ madhumattamaḥ sutaḥ soma ṛtāvṛdhā | tam aśvinā pibataṃ tiroahnyaṃ dhattaṃ ratnāni dāśuṣe || 1 ||

Pada-pāṭha

अयम् । वाम् । मधुमत्ऽतमः । सुतः । सोमः । ऋतऽवृधा । तम् । अश्विना । पिबतम् । तिरःऽअह्न्यम् । धत्तम् । रत्नानि । दाशुषे ॥ १ ॥

ayam | vām | madhumat-tamaḥ | sutaḥ | somaḥ | ṛta-vṛdhā | tam | aśvinā | pibatam | tiraḥ-ahnyam | dhattam | ratnāni | dāśuṣe || 1 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे ऋतावृधा ऋतस्य सत्यस्य यज्ञस्य वा वर्धयितारावश्विना अश्विनौ वां युवयोरयं पुरोवर्ती सोमः सुतोऽभिषुतः । कीदृशः । मधुमत्तमोऽतिशयेन माधुर्यवान् । तिरोअह्न्यं तिरोभूते पूर्वस्मिन्नहनि अभिषुतं तं सोमं पिबतं । दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते यजमानाय रत्नानि रमणीयानि धनानि धत्तं । प्रयच्छतम् ॥

he ṛtāvṛdhā ṛtasya satyasya yajñasya vā vardhayitārāv aśvinā aśvinau vāṃ yuvayor ayaṃ purovartī somaḥ suto 'bhiṣutaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ | madhumattamo 'tiśayena mādhuryavān | tiroahnyaṃ tirobhūte pūrvasminn ahani abhiṣutaṃ taṃ somaṃ pibataṃ | dāśuṣe havir dattavate yajamānāya ratnāni ramaṇīyāni dhanāni dhattaṃ | prayacchatam ||

Translation: "O ṛtāvṛdhā, increasers of truth or of the sacrifice, O Aśvins: ayam, this Soma lying before (you), vām, yours, is sutaḥ, pressed. Of what kind? Madhumattamaḥ, exceedingly sweet. Tiroahnyam: pressed on the previous, vanished day — tam somam pibatam, drink that Soma. Dāśuṣe, to the sacrificer who has given the oblation, ratnāni, delightful riches, dhattam, give (prayacchatam)."

Grammatical tail characterized, numerals as read [?] - vām: for the genitive dual of yuṣmad, vām by yuṣmadasmadoḥ ṣaṣṭhīcaturthīdvitīyāsthayor vāṃnāvau (Pā. 8-1-20 as read [?]); it is unaccented. - madhumattamaḥ: root mana jñāne; "manyate, he who knows" = madhu; the suffix u by phalipāṭinami…; initial acute by the continued "nit"; dh as an end-substitute; "madhumān, exceedingly" = madhumattamaḥ with matup and tamap; both being pit, they are unaccented and only the word-accent remains. - ṛtāvṛdhā: root vṛdh, with the causative sense included, kvip; by anyeṣām api dṛśyate the first member lengthens. - tiroahnyam: ahni bhavaḥ = ahnyaḥ; yat by bhave chandasi; the ṭi-loss is excluded by ahnaṣṭakhoreva (Pā. 6-4-144 as read [?]); nas taddhite therefore does not drop the ṭi; the prakṛtibhāva by ye cābhāvakarmaṇoḥ (Pā. 6-4-168 as read [?]) is optional in the Chandas and does not come; alloponaḥ drops the a; "tirohito 'hnyaḥ"; tiro 'ntardhau (Pā. 1-4-71 as read [?]) gives gati-status, indeclinable; the compound with an indeclinable first member keeps its accent. - dāśuṣe: dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca (as printed): the kvasu-ending word given by nipātana; in the dative singular, saṃprasāraṇa of vasu (Pā. 6-4-131 as read [?]); ṣatva by śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca.

Pratipadārtha — "ṛtāvṛdhā — O promoters of the sacrifice or of truth; aśvinā — O Aśvin gods; vām — for you two; madhumattamaḥ — most sweet; ayaṃ somaḥ — this Soma juice; sutaḥ — has been pressed; tiroahnyam — pressed on the day before (yesterday); tam — that Soma juice; pibatam — drink; dāśuṣe — to the sacrificer who offers the oblation; ratnāni — delightful riches; dhattam — give."

Bhāvārtha — "O Aśvin gods, you promote the sacrifice or truth. For you this Soma juice was made ready on the very day before. Drink this exceedingly sweet Soma juice. Give delightful, mind-gladdening riches to the sacrificer who offers the oblation."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 3) — "O Aswins, encouragers of sacrifice, this most sweet Soma juice is pre-pared [sic: line-break hyphen, "pre-pared", printed in the line "is pre-" / "pared"] for you; it is of yesterday's expressing ; drink it and grant riches to the sacrificer"

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 4 the heading is printed "viśeṣa viṣayagaḷu" - ṛtāvṛdhā — "promoters of truth or of the sacrifice. We have already explained the meaning of this word." - tiroahnyam — "tirobhūte pūrvasmin dine; tirohito 'hnyas tiroahnyaḥ: the day that has gone by, the previous day, yesterday." - dāśuṣe — "havirdattavate yajamānāya: to the sacrificer who gives the oblation."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 4–6 — grammar pages, noted briefly - vām: the genitive dual ending of yuṣmad ("yuvayoḥ"); yuṣmadasmadoḥ ṣaṣṭhīcaturthīdvitīyāsthayor vāṃnāvau (Pā. 8-1-20 as read [?]) — युष्मदस्मदोः षष्ठीचतुर्थीद्वितीयास्थयोर्वांनावौ — the genitive, dative and accusative dual forms of yuṣmad and asmad, standing after a word and not at the beginning of a pāda, are replaced by vām and nau, and are unaccented; the Kannada author notes that tvā, mā in the singular and vas, nas in the plural exist, so that the dual forms vām, nau remain for this rule. - madhumattamaḥ: root mana jñāne; the Uṇādi rule phalipāṭinamijanāṃ gukpaṭinākiteś ca (Uṇ. 1-[?]8 as read [?]) — फलिपाटिनमिजनां गुक्पटिनाकितेश्च — the suffix u, being nit; with guk for phal, paṭi for pāṭ, nāki for nam, a th for the n of man and t for the n of jan; so after mana, u, with dh for n: madhu; ñnityādir nityam (Pā. 6-1-197 as read [?]) gives the initial acute. "Madhu asya asti": tadasyāsty asminn iti matup (Pā. 5-2-94 as read [?]); for "excess", atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau (Pā. 5-3-55 as read [?]) gives tamap; matup and tamap are both pit and therefore unaccented (anudāttau suppitau, Pā. 3-1-4 as read [?]); the initial acute that belonged to madhu stays, the rest becomes non-acute; udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ gives the svarita to the thu after the acute; the rest follow svaritāt saṃhitāyām anudāttānām. - ṛtāvṛdhā: although there is no ṇic, the root vṛdhu vardhane has the sense of it; kvip ca (Pā. 3-2-76 as read [?]) gives kvip; all letters of the suffix drop; anyeṣām api dṛśyate (Pā. 6-3-137 as read [?]) lengthens the first member, ṛta, as it is seen to lengthen other first members besides those listed from nipāta and so on; in the vocative dual the ending au is ā (supāṃ suluk…): ṛtāvṛdhā. - tiroahnyam: ahni bhavaḥ — "belonging to the day"; bhave chandasi (Pā. 4-4-110 as read [?]) gives yat; ahan + ya; ahnaṣṭakhoreva (Pā. 6-4-144 as read [?]) — the ṭi of ahan drops only before ṭa and kha; so, with other suffixes, no ṭi-loss, and nas taddhite (Pā. 6-4-144 as read [?]) does not apply; alloponaḥ (Pā. 6-4-134 as read [?]) drops the a of an; ye cābhāvakarmaṇoḥ (Pā. 6-4-168 as read [?]) would require prakṛtibhāva; but sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante (Paribhāṣā, "63" as read [?]) makes it optional, so it does not come. Tiras + ahnya; sasajuṣo ruḥ; ato ror aplutād aplute gives u; ād guṇaḥ; tiro 'ntardhau (Pā. 1-4-71 as read [?]) — tiras in the sense of "concealment" is a gati (the Kannada author notes that it is read in the svar-ādi list); then svarādinipātam avyayam gives the name avyaya; and tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā… (Pā. 6-2-2 as read [?]) gives the indeclinable first member its natural accent. - dāśuṣe: root dāś dāne; dāśvān sāhvān mīḍhvāṃś ca (Pā. 6-1-12 as read [?]) — the forms dāśvān, sāhvān, mīḍhvān are given by nipātana as ending in kvasu; in three places the doubling is absent, and the iṭ-augment is absent in some and present in others; in the second the parasmaipada and the lengthening of the penultimate are also given by nipātana; dāś + vas: dāśvas; jas; in the dative singular, vasoḥ saṃprasāraṇam (Pā. 6-4-131 as read [?]) — saṃprasāraṇa (v → u) of the aṅga ending in vasu and having the bha-designation; u and the pūrvarūpa; ādeśapratyayayoḥ (Pā. 8-3-59 as read) gives ṣ for s; śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca (Pā. 8-3-60 as read [?]) — here the Kannada author discusses at length whether vas in this sūtra refers to the root vasa nivāse or to the suffix vasu, and, by the maxim "sahacaritāsahacaritayoḥ sahacaritasyaiva grahaṇam" (Paribhāṣā, "113" as read [?]), concludes that the root is intended; and that the Kaumudī uses this sūtra in treating the root vasa nivāse in the first class so as to avoid confusion; the argument is outlined, not transcribed. || 1 ||

original p. 6

Rik 2

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

त्रिवन्धुरेण त्रिवृता सुपेशसा रथेना यातमश्विना । कण्वासो वां ब्रह्म कृण्वन्त्यध्वरे तेषां सु शृणुतं हवम् ॥ २ ॥

trivandhureṇa trivṛtā supeśasā rathenā yātam aśvinā | kaṇvāso vāṃ brahma kṛṇvanty adhvare teṣāṃ su śṛṇutaṃ havam || 2 || The print reads trivandhureṇa with v throughout — the usual form is tribandhura; It is given as printed [?].

Pada-pāṭha

त्रिऽवन्धुरेण । त्रिऽवृता । सुऽपेशसा । रथेन । आ । यातम् । अश्विना । कण्वासः । वाम् । ब्रह्म । कृण्वन्ति । अध्वरे । तेषाम् । सु । शृणुतम् । हवम् ॥ २ ॥

tri-vandhureṇa | tri-vṛtā | su-peśasā | rathena | ā | yātam | aśvinā | kaṇvāsaḥ | vām | brahma | kṛṇvanti | adhvare | teṣām | su | śṛṇutam | havam || 2 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे अश्विना त्रिवन्धुरेणोन्नतानतरूपत्रिविधबन्धनकाष्ठयुक्तेन । त्रिवृताप्रतिहतगतिकया लोकत्रये वर्तमानेन सुपेशसा शोभनसुवर्णयुक्तेन रथेना यातं । इहागच्छतं । कण्वासः कण्वपुत्रा मेधाविन ऋत्विजो वा वां युवयोरध्वरे योगे ब्रह्म स्तोत्ररूपं मन्त्रं हविर्लक्षणमन्नं वा कृण्वन्ति । कुर्वन्ति । तेषां कण्वानां हवमाह्वानं सु शृणुतं । सुष्ठ्वादरेण शृणुतम् ॥ त्रिवन्धुरेण । बध्नन्तीति बन्धुराः । बन्धेरौणादिक उरन्प्रत्ययः । त्रयो बन्धुरा यस्यासौ त्रिबन्धुरः । त्रिचक्रादिषु पाठात् त्रिचक्रादीनां छन्दस्युपसंख्यानं । पा. ६-२-१९९-१ [?] । इत्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । त्रिवृता । त्रिषु लोकेषु वर्तत इति त्रिवृत् । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । सुपेशसा । पेश इति हिरण्यनाम । शोभनं पेशो यस्यासौ सुपेशाः । आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । शृणुतं । श्रु श्रवणे । श्रुवः शृ च । तत्सन्नियोगेन धातोः शृभावश्च । हवं । ह्वयतेर्भावेऽनुपसर्गस्य । पा. ३-३-७३ [?] । इत्यप् । संप्रसारणं च गुणावादेशौ । प्रत्ययस्य पित्त्वादनुदात्तत्वे धातुस्वरः ॥

he aśvinā trivandhureṇonnatānatarūpatrividhabandhanakāṣṭhayuktena | trivṛtāpratihatagatikayā lokatraye vartamānena supeśasā śobhanasuvarṇayuktena rathenā yātaṃ | ihāgacchataṃ | kaṇvāsaḥ kaṇvaputrā medhāvina ṛtvijo vā vāṃ yuvayor adhvare yoge brahma stotrarūpaṃ mantraṃ havirlakṣaṇam annaṃ vā kṛṇvanti | kurvanti | teṣāṃ kaṇvānāṃ havam āhvānaṃ su śṛṇutaṃ | suṣṭhv ādareṇa śṛṇutam || trivandhureṇa | badhnantīti bandhurāḥ | bandherauṇādika uranpratyayaḥ | trayo bandhurā yasyāsau tribandhuraḥ | tricakrādiṣu pāṭhāt tricakrādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānaṃ | pā. 6-2-199-1 [?] | ity uttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | trivṛtā | triṣu lokeṣu vartata iti trivṛt | kvip ceti kvip | supeśasā | peśa iti hiraṇyanāma | śobhanaṃ peśo yasyāsau supeśāḥ | ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasīty uttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | śṛṇutaṃ | śru śravaṇe | śruvaḥ śṛ ca | tatsanniyogena dhātoḥ śṛbhāvaś ca | havaṃ | hvayater bhāve 'nupasargasya | pā. 3-3-73 [?] | ity ap | saṃprasāraṇaṃ ca guṇāvādeśau | pratyayasya pittvād anudāttatve dhātusvaraḥ ||

Translation: "O Aśvins, trivandhureṇa, with your chariot furnished with three kinds of fastening-pieces of wood, raised, lowered [and the like]; trivṛtā, going with unhindered course through the three worlds; supeśasā, with fine gold: ā yātam, come here. Kaṇvāsaḥ, the Kaṇvas — sons of Kaṇva, wise priests — vām, in your adhvare, sacrifice, brahma kṛṇvanti, make (the mantra in the form of praise, or food in the form of the oblation). Teṣām, of those Kaṇvas, havam, the call, su śṛṇutam, hear well, with full regard. Trivandhureṇa: 'those that bind are bandhurāḥ'; the Uṇādi suffix uran after bandh; 'he who has three bandhuras'; by listing under tricakra etc., the upasaṃkhyāna for the tricakra class in the Chandas (Pā. 6-2-199 vārttika [?]) gives the end of the second member the acute. Trivṛtā: 'who exists in the three worlds', kvip. Supeśasā: peśa is a name of gold; 'he who has fine gold'; the second member is initial-acute. Śṛṇutam: root śru śravaṇe, śṛ for the root with śru; havam: from hve, in the abstract sense without a prefix, ap (Pā. 3-3-73 [?]); saṃprasāraṇa, guṇa, āv-substitution; the suffix being pit, the accent is that of the root." On the sense of "adhvare … brahma" in the bhāṣya, the printed text reads yoge ("in your yoga") for yajñe, as read, [?]; given as printed.

Rik 47.2, continued from p. 7

Pratipadārtha — "aśvinā — O Aśvin gods; trivandhureṇa — beautiful with three seats (or posts); trivṛtā — (since it has no obstruction) moving in the three worlds (going about them); supeśasā — made of excellent gold; rathena — with the chariot; āyātam — come (here); kaṇvāsaḥ — the sons of Kaṇva or wise priests; vām — to you; adhvare — in the sacrifice; brahma — a mantra in the form of praise, or food in the form of the oblation; kṛṇvanti — make (offer); teṣām — of those sons of Kaṇva or wise priests; havam — the invocation; su śṛṇutam — hear with regard."

Bhāvārtha — "O Aśvin gods, come to this place of sacrifice, seated in your chariot, which is made of excellent gold, is beautiful with three seats, and moves in the three worlds without obstruction. Here the sons of Kaṇva, or wise priests, offer you, in the sacrifice, mantras in the form of praise or food in the form of the oblation. Hear their invocation with regard."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 7) — "Come hither, O Aswins, in your triangular and beautiful car of the three-fold pole. The Kanwas compose and ^repeat [sic: the first letter of "repeat" is printed raised] your praise at the sacrifice ; Kindly hear their invocation."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 7–8 - "In this ṛk the form of the chariot of the Aśvin gods is described. Trivandhureṇa trivṛtā rathena: the idea is that their chariot is triangular in shape and has three posts. The commentator explains the word trivṛtā as 'having unobstructed motion in the three worlds'. This manner of describing the chariot of the Aśvin gods is seen in several places in the Ṛgveda. For example:" — three Ṛgveda citations, untranslated in the source; each is given in three layers, with an editorial and tentative gloss, references "as read [?]":

  1. त्रिवन्धुरेण त्रिवृता रथेन त्रिचक्रेण सुवृता यातमर्वाक् ॥ Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-118-2 as read [?]

    trivandhureṇa trivṛtā rathena tricakreṇa suvṛtā yātam arvāk || — editorial and tentative: "Come hither with your chariot of the three seats, the threefold, three-wheeled, well-rolling one."

  2. त्रिवन्धुरेण त्रिवृता रथेना यातमश्विना ॥ Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-8-[?] as read [?]

    trivandhureṇa trivṛtā rathenā yātam aśvinā || — editorial and tentative: "Come, O Aśvins, with the three-seated, threefold chariot." (the line is the same as the first half of this Rik 2)

  3. अर्वाङ् त्रिचक्रो मधुवाहनो रथो जीराश्वो अश्विनोर्यातु सुष्टुतः । त्रिवन्धुरो मघवा विश्वसौभगः शं न आ वक्षद्द्विपदे चतुष्पदे ॥ Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-157-3 as read [?]

    arvāṅ tricakro madhuvāhano ratho jīrāśvo aśvinor yātu suṣṭutaḥ | trivandhuro maghavā viśvasaubhagaḥ śaṃ na ā vakṣad dvipade catuṣpade || — editorial and tentative: "May the Aśvins' well-praised chariot, three-wheeled, honey-bearing, drawn by swift horses, come this way; three-seated, bountiful, bringing all good fortune, may it bring well-being to us, to our bipeds and quadrupeds."

"In these ṛks, the chariot of the Aśvin gods is described in many places as having three wheels. Therefore, in describing the chariot of the Aśvin gods, the words trivandhura, trivṛt and tricakra have been used by many sages, and so it can be understood that these words have a definite meaning." - kaṇvāsaḥ — "medhāvino ṛtvijaḥ: wise priests; or the sons of the sage Kaṇva; the descendants of the sage Kaṇva." - brahma — "among the twenty-eight [?] names of food beginning andhaḥ, vājaḥ, the word brahma is read, so brahma means food (Ni. 2-[?] as read); and among the twenty-eight [?] names of wealth beginning rekṇaḥ, the word brahma is read, so brahma means wealth (Ni. 2-[?] as read); and, according to (Ni. 13-[?] as read), brahma means stotra: three meanings. Here any of the meanings may be given."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 8–9 — grammar pages, noted briefly - tribandhureṇa the print here spells the first member with b: "tribanduraṇa" / "tribandhura": root bandha bandhane; "badhnanti iti bandhurāḥ"; the Uṇādi suffix uran; "trayaḥ bandhurāḥ yasya saḥ", a bahuvrīhi meaning "having a carriage of wood tied in three ways". Bandhura by the nit-accent is initial-acute; tri by the prātipadika accent is end-acute; after the compound is formed, bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam (Pā. 6-2-1 as read) would give the first member's natural accent; but in the section on end-acute (antodātta), the vārttika "tricakrādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam" (Pā. 6-2-199 vārttika, as read "6-2-199-1" [?]) — "tricakra and the like are to be added in the Chandas" — gives the end of such words as tricakra and tribandhura the acute in the Chandas; this overrides the first member's natural accent, giving end-acute. - trivṛtā: "triṣu lokeṣu vartate", "is in the three worlds"; after the root vṛtu vartane, with tri as upapada, kvip; instrumental singular. - supeśasā: peśa is a name for gold; "śobhanaṃ peśaḥ yasya saḥ", "having fine gold"; ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi (Pā. 6-1-119 as read [?]) — a second member of two vowels, after su, is initial-acute in the Chandas; here, after the root piśa dīpane, the Uṇādi suffix asun, so peśas is initial-acute. - śṛṇutam: root śru śravaṇe, loṭ, second person dual thas; loṭo laṅvat gives laṅ-likeness; tasthasthamipāṃ tāṃtaṃtāmaḥ (Pā. 3-4-101 as read [?]) gives tam; śru + ta; śruvaḥ śṛ ca (Pā. 3-1-74 as read [?]) — श्रुवः शृ च — before a kartṛ-sense sārvadhātuka suffix in the Vedic, śṛ is substituted for śru and śnu comes as the vikaraṇa in place of śap: śṛ + nu + ta; the Kannada author says that both substitute and vikaraṇa are "left over together" (sanniyogaśiṣṭa), so both come in a single act; ur nuvarṇāt [i.e. nor ṇatvaṃ, as printed — crowded [?]] gives the n its ṇ: śṛṇutam. - havam: root hveñ spardhāyāṃ śabde ca; bhāve 'nupasargasya (Pā. 3-3-70 as read [?]) — भावेऽनुपसर्गस्य — in the abstract sense, for a root without a prefix, saṃprasāraṇa of hve (v → u) and the suffix ap; hu + e + a, pūrvarūpa: hu + a; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ gives guṇa: u → o; āv in place of that o; accusative singular am: havam; the suffix ap is pit and the case-ending is sup, so both are unaccented (anudāttau suppitau), and the root-accent alone remains. || 2 ||
